name: Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Reservoir, boat safaris and forest safaris at the Agasthya foothills
summary: Reservoir-backed sanctuary near Thiruvananthapuram offering boat safaris, lion and crocodile parks and guided treks; post-monsoon winter (Nov–Feb) is drier and comfortable for lake boating and…
description: Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary protects forest and reservoir country at the foot of the Agasthyamala (Agasthya) hills. The site combines a dam and lake, lion and crocodile display/rehabilitation areas, watch towers and forested trails that lead into the Western Ghats foothills. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_Dam?utm_source=openai))

The Kerala Forest Department runs regulated activities from the dam/boat-landing station: boat safaris (including jumbo/long cruises), bus/jeep safaris, and ecotourism trekking packages that use the lake as a gateway to deeper trails. Visitors see deer, macaques, birds and sometimes giant squirrels or other Western Ghats species along the shoreline. ([staging.forest.kerala.gov.in](https://staging.forest.kerala.gov.in/forestapp/public/documents/publications/file0211202407%3A39%3A04.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Weather and access make winter (post-monsoon) the comfortable season: November to February are cooler and drier, improving visibility on the water and making trails easier to manage for safaris and boating. Always confirm specific programmes and bookings with the forest office before you travel. ([roampedia.com](https://roampedia.com/india/kerala/thiruvananthapuram/thiruvananthapuram-city/place/neyyar-trek?section=stay&utm_source=openai))
highlights: Boat safaris on Neyyar reservoir (short and jumbo options run by Forest Dept).
Lion safari park, deer watching zone and Crocodile Rehabilitation & Research Centre.
Forest treks to Kombai and Meenmutty falls accessible from the boat landing.
Easy day-trip from Thiruvananthapuram (about 25–35 km by road).
Post-monsoon to late-winter is the best season for boating and safaris.

sections.heading: Background
body: Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary was established to protect the forested catchment of the Neyyar River and the reservoir at Neyyar Dam, and forms part of the Agasthyamala biosphere landscape. The reservoir is both a water resource and the focal point for many visitor activities. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_Dam?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Boat safaris: Forest Department boat safaris patrol the reservoir edge and deliver views of shoreline wildlife and forest-clad hills; there are also jumbo/long-boat cruise options and point-to-point cruises that link to trekking start points. Fees and permitted group sizes are set by the Forest Department; book at the sanctuary office. ([staging.forest.kerala.gov.in](https://staging.forest.kerala.gov.in/forestapp/public/documents/publications/file0211202407%3A39%3A04.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Wildlife displays and parks: close to the dam visitors find a lion safari park (managed/exhibit), a deer viewing area and a crocodile rehabilitation and research centre—these are useful for families and those who want a quick wildlife experience without deep treks. ([dtpcthiruvananthapuram.com](https://www.dtpcthiruvananthapuram.com/destination/neyyar-wildlife-sanctuary?utm_source=openai))

Trekking and Kombai boat+walk routes: Ekotourism packages combine a short boat ride to Kombai with multi-kilometre treks to Meenmutty Falls or deeper forest routes. These run seasonally and require prior booking through the Kerala Forest/eco-tourism office. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/ecotourism/trekking-programs/neyyar-packages/21?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: November–March (post-monsoon and winter) — drier trails, cooler mornings and calm water make boating and safaris comfortable. Avoid the heavy-monsoon months (June–September) when many programmes close or run at reduced capacity. ([roampedia.com](https://roampedia.com/india/kerala/thiruvananthapuram/thiruvananthapuram-city/place/neyyar-trek?section=stay&utm_source=openai))

Booking and permits: safaris, boat cruises and guided treks operate under Forest Department control; walk-in boat rides may be available but organised safaris and trekking packages should be booked in advance at the sanctuary/eco-tourism desk. Confirm current fees, timings and group rules with the Neyyar office before you travel. ([staging.forest.kerala.gov.in](https://staging.forest.kerala.gov.in/forestapp/public/documents/publications/file0211202407%3A39%3A04.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Getting there: Neyyar Dam and the sanctuary are roughly 30 km east of Thiruvananthapuram city. Reach by private car or KSRTC/private buses to Kattakada/Neyyar Dam; taxis and hired cars from the city are the most convenient for morning safaris. ([dtpcthiruvananthapuram.com](https://www.dtpcthiruvananthapuram.com/destination/neyyar-wildlife-sanctuary?utm_source=openai))

latest.text: Draft Gazette notification publishes an eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) proposal for Neyyar-Peppara area; this may affect zoning and permitted activities—confirm any changes before planning specialist activities.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November to March (post‑monsoon dry months; winter mornings are cool and ideal for boating and safaris).
visitorInfo.howToReach: About 25–35 km from Thiruvananthapuram by road (KSRTC and private buses serve the area); nearest rail and air hub is Thiruvananthapuram—hire a taxi or take a local bus to Neyyar Dam/boat landing. ([dtpcthiruvananthapuram.com](https://www.dtpcthiruvananthapuram.com/destination/neyyar-wildlife-sanctuary?utm_source=openai))
etiquette: Confirm boat-safari or trek bookings with the Forest Department / eco-tourism office before you go; many programmes require advance booking. ([staging.forest.kerala.gov.in](https://staging.forest.kerala.gov.in/forestapp/public/documents/publications/file0211202407%3A39%3A04.pdf?utm_source=openai))
Morning safaris give the best light and cooler temperatures; carry water, sun protection and insect repellent.

If you plan a Kombai boat + trek to Meenmutty Falls, wear sturdy shoes and check trail status — trails run seasonally and can close in monsoon. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/ecotourism/trekking-programs/neyyar-packages/21?utm_source=openai))
